items.title: OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY RISK ASSESSMENT DURING PURSE SEINE VESSEL UNLOADING OPERATIONS AT KUTARAJA OCEANIC FISHING PORT, ACEH
items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of preventing workplace accidents and illnesses, particularly during high-risk vessel unloading operations at the Kutaraja Oceanic Fishing Port (OFP) in Banda Aceh. Inadequate implementation of safety programs, such as hazard identification, risk analysis, and risk control, is a primary cause of workplace accidents in this sector. This study aimed to identify activities and analyze occupational safety risks associated with the unloading process of purse seine vessels at OFP Kutaraja over one month, focusing on seven vessels. The methodology involved direct observation, interviews with crew members, and data analysis using the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) approach. Risk assessment was conducted using a risk matrix that factored in both severity and probability. The results indicate that the unloading operation comprises three main stages: pre-unloading, the unloading process, and post-unloading. Each stage presents varying levels of risk, ranging from "Acceptable" to "Unacceptable". The highest risks were associated with handling fish-filled brail nets and transporting the catch, activities that carry the potential for serious accidents. Contributing risk factors included the lack of use of personal protective equipment (PPE), suboptimal work procedures, and unsafe working conditions. Safety during vessel unloading operations could be improved through regular training, increased PPE usage, and the implementation of a JSA-based risk control system.

items.title: Occupational Visual Strain and Associated Ergonomic Risk Factors Among Watchmakers: A Cross-Sectional Study of Binocular Vision, Ocular Pain and Intraocular Pressure
items.abstract: Background: Watch repairing involves prolonged near-vision activity, monocular loupe use, sustained convergence, awkward postures, and repetitive fine motor movements, potentially contributing to ocular strain. The ocular and ergonomic impact of such occupations has not yet been documented. Objective: To study the ocular stress profile along with ergonomics risk factors among male watchmakers from Kolkata, India. Methods: This comparative cross-sectional study included 140 men aged 40–50 years, comprising 70 watchmakers with over 15 years of occupational exposure and 70 controls. Visual pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS), near point of convergence (NPC) and accommodation using the RAF rule, fusional vergence using a prism bar, ocular movements using a synoptophore, intraocular pressure (IOP) using non-contact tonometry, and visual acuity using a Snellen chart. Fundus photography and ergonomic assessments were also performed. Data were analysed using independent-samples t-tests (SPSS version 26; p<0.05). Results: Watchmakers exhibited significantly greater visual pain (7.29±0.58 cm vs. 3.81±0.30 cm; p<0.001) and receded NPC (16.57±1.51 cm vs. 7.86±1.35 cm; p<0.001), both remaining significant after Holm correction. Adduction was reduced (p=0.010), whereas IOP was higher in both eyes (p=0.044). Visual acuity and anthropometric differences were statistically insignificant. Major ergonomic concerns included inadequate rest periods, monocular loupe use, postural strain, and hand discomfort. Conclusion: Prolonged monocular near work by watchmakers can lead to convergence insufficiency-like symptoms, increased eye pain, and increased intraocular pressure. It is necessary for ergonomic measures such as using bi-ocular devices and proper work rest cycles and eye screenings to be taken.

items.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics
items.abstract: Computational biologists increasingly delegate substantial analyses to AI agents in long-horizon, multi-turn sessions, yet most benchmarks of agents' bioinformatics capabilities pose a single short task with a single-shot prompt. We present OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark for AI agents. Each of its 97 tasks links dependent subtasks into a directed acyclic graph, for 662 underlying subtasks in all. Each subtask is posed as one user turn and graded deterministically against an answer key, with optional in-context feedback on incorrect answers. Across 12 models on three harnesses, the slowest agent averages 3.6 hours per task, and no combination comes near saturating the benchmark, with mean scores of 0.43 to 0.57 out of a possible 1 without in-context feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Multi-turn evaluation also uncovers behavior that single-shot prompts cannot, as agents score lower on subtasks that depend on earlier subtasks, and in-context feedback helps agents recover some of that loss. Because deterministic scoring gives no qualitative account of how an agent failed, we also introduce an unsupervised failure mode discovery pipeline that describes, embeds, and clusters agents' failed attempts to surface emergent failure modes. Applied to OmicsBench, this pipeline exposes qualitative shortcomings in how agents carry out bioinformatics analyses, ranging from agents applying their own statistical filters in place of the specified ones to agents writing whole answers from memory.

items.title: Onboard Lightweight LLM Reasoning for Human-Aware Safe UAV Navigation
items.abstract: Aerial robots operating near people must treat a pedestrian, a parked car, and a wall differently, yet conventional perception--planning stacks reduce all of them to occupied geometry---a \emph{human-aware safety gap} in which category-specific clearance is unavailable to the planner and temporary occlusions remove pedestrian-specific constraints from its map. We present a modular, fully onboard pipeline that closes this gap by turning visual observations into context-dependent safety constraints for real-time UAV navigation. A shared BLIP encoder drives scene captioning and text-conditioned segmentation, which is fused with depth to localize obstacles in 3D. Obstacle-specific risk is inferred by a lightweight LLM (Qwen-2.5-0.5B) stabilized with retrieval-augmented generation and grammar-constrained decoding that restricts its output to a planner-compatible JSON schema. The LLM reasons once per object category rather than per frame: its verdicts are cached per class, so previously seen categories are resolved without inference and new ones trigger a fresh retrieval-grounded query; detections are additionally given persistent identities and held in the map across occlusions. The perception pipeline runs at 10\,Hz on a Jetson Orin NX, while fallback LLM queries take approximately 0.8\,s and remain off the control-critical path. In Gazebo, low-altitude urban navigation among pedestrians and vehicles shows a roughly $3\times$ reduction in collision events over a geometric planner, and semantics-aware landing among moving actors raises success from 34\% to 96\%. The 224-pixel encoder input limits reliable small-object perception at range; conservative pedestrian margins and short-term persistence mitigate this limitation during navigation.

items.title: OntoAct: Hypothesis-Based Neuro-Symbolic Agents through Ontological Abstraction
items.abstract: Learning from experience requires recovering reusable knowledge and determining when it applies to a new situation. We introduce OntoAct, a hypothesis-based neuro-symbolic framework built on ontological abstraction. OntoAct turns individual experiences into axioms over entity types, relations, and conditions, making their underlying patterns reusable across situations. A large language model (LLM) uses this world knowledge to propose hypotheses and actions, while a symbolic verifier assesses their supporting conditions against current observations. Verification identifies missing evidence, and new observations and intervention outcomes update hypothesis assessments and guide subsequent actions. We also introduce Tacit-FLE, a benchmark built on the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE) for diagnosing and repairing hidden faults in existing factories using inherited operational records. Its synthetic maintenance corpus distributes evidence across records, and an executed repair may leave the fault unresolved, requiring agents to reassess their diagnoses through interaction. Across Tacit-FLE, Mars, and ALFWorld, OntoAct achieves leading task performance with efficient interaction and inference.

items.title: Operation Dark Clark: AI‑Enabled Russian Disinformation in Latin America and the Campaign to Shape Brazilian Politics (2020–2026)
items.abstract: This thesis reconstructs and critically evaluates Operation Dark Clark, a Russia-origin influence operation that OpenAI reportedly disrupted and publicly documented on 8 October 2026. It assesses the operation as the first influence campaign ever classified by the company in Category 5 of the IO Breakout Scale—its highest rating for a disrupted operation—and the most complex false-front identity it had dismantled in two and a half years of systematic reporting. The operation combined generative artificial intelligence with classical intelligence tradecraft. It recruited unwitting employees in Latin America to staff a seemingly legitimate organization called the “Social Research Center” (SRC), which was controlled through a fabricated persona named “Mia Clark.” Her published corpus comprised more than sixty original research articles examining public opinion on BRICS and comparing the Brazilian economy under Presidents Jair Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Drawing on an open-source intelligence (OSINT) verification protocol that distinguishes documented and verified facts from attributed claims and editorial speculation, the thesis traces the operation’s activities across Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Panama, and Brazil. It reconstructs the operation’s institutional lineage, from Soviet active measures through the Internet Research Agency, PeaceData (2020), and the Prigozhin-linked “Politology”/“La Compañia” network, reportedly now under the control of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR). The study situates the case within the broader industrialization of AI-enabled information confrontation, examining the contemporaneous Iranian “Bogus Bylines” operation and the transnational Pravda network. A dedicated chapter investigates the October 2026 Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centers and the observed 94% collapse in automated traffic across the Yandex network, cautioning against unwarranted causal interpretations of the relationship between these events. The thesis argues that Dark Clark represents a doctrinal evolution from platform-based amplification toward institutional laundering: the introduction of synthetic or co-opted authority into established media organizations and academic institutions. It contends that effective democratic resilience requires a multilayered response combining platform transparency, institutional source verification, provenance standards, and robust fact-checking capacity. The analysis deliberately refrains from endorsing the unverified assertion circulating in Brazilian political commentary that the operation materially influenced Brazilian electoral outcomes.

items.title: Operational Gaps in Remote ID: Implications for Real-Time UAS Surveillance and Airspace Safety
items.abstract: Remote ID has emerged as a foundational capability for enabling accountability, situational awareness, and scalable integration of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) into the national airspace. While current regulatory frameworks emphasize Remote ID as a key component of future UAS operations, limited discussion has focused on how Remote ID data performs under real operational monitoring conditions. This presentation examines the practical reliability of Remote ID for real-time UAS surveillance and highlights several operational limitations that affect tracking continuity, detection confidence, and airspace awareness. The study presents a data-driven evaluation framework developed to analyze high frequency Remote ID observations alongside external UAS detection and telemetry data streams. The framework incorporates second-level temporal synchronization, geospatial matching, duplicate-event handling, and event-driven detection analysis to assess how inconsistencies in Remote ID broadcasts influence monitoring performance. Attention is given to issues such as timestamp irregularities, intermittent signal loss, identity ambiguity, and spatial inaccuracies resulting from differing positional reference systems and broadcast conditions. Results demonstrate that even small temporal or positional inconsistencies can significantly impact real-time surveillance reliability, particularly in dense or safety-sensitive operational environments. The presentation further discusses how these limitations may affect counter-UAS operations, enforcement workflows, Unmanned Aircraft System Traffic Management (UTM) integration, and broader airspace safety initiatives. Rather than positioning Remote ID as a standalone surveillance solution, the findings support a layered monitoring architecture in which Remote ID is integrated with complementary sensing modalities such as radar, RF detection, and network-based tracking systems. In addition to identifying operational gaps, the presentation proposes several recommendations aimed at improving the reliability and interoperability of Remote ID based monitoring systems. These include improved timestamp standardization, enhanced broadcast consistency requirements, and more rigorous validation methodologies for evaluating real-time detection performance. The goal of this work is to provide government, industry, and academic stakeholders with a practical assessment of the current capabilities and limitations of Remote ID as the UAS ecosystem continues to expand.

items.title: Operationalizing AI Governance for Defense SMEs: A Modular, Generative-AI-Assisted Framework for NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC Compliance
items.abstract: This praxis investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) governance can be integrated into the cybersecurity compliance workflows of United States defense small and mid-sized enterprises (SMEs). These firms are navigating the transition to the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 program and the foundational requirements of National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-171. Existing AI risk guidance, such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), does not provide implementation-focused direction suited to the resource constraints of smaller firms. This praxis therefore describes a control mapping method consistent with the overlay logic of NIST's Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems (COSAIS) concept paper. It uses that method to develop the Modular AI Governance Framework (MAGF), a "comply once, satisfy many" governance framework and toolkit. My research uses a convergent mixed-methods design guided by five research questions. Four ask how practitioners map AI risk categories to control families, which families they identify most often, how feasible they judge lightweight governance artifacts to be, and what barriers and enablers shape implementation. The fifth asks to what extent the resulting framework is practical, scalable, and audit-aligned. In the first phase, 38 practitioners mapped six AI risk categories onto the 14 NIST SP 800-171 control families through a structured survey. They prioritized "auditability gaps" in data integrity and model transparency, yet many reported lacking the specialized staff to document these areas manually. Qualitative analysis of their open-ended responses produced eight empirically grounded design requirements, including control family anchoring, traceability-first evidence, change control for probabilistic systems, and a dual-purpose evidence pattern. Inspired by operational "playbooks," the MAGF defines governance tasks as structured modules with goals, actions, and lightweight evidence artifacts. The modules model the work already required in defense cybersecurity and span the AI lifecycle from initiation and data collection to production deployment and monitoring. A prompt library provides engineered prompts for generative AI chatbot tools like Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot to support human-reviewed drafting of artifacts such as bias assessment records and model/prompt change logs. No output of that prompt library was evaluated in this study. I evaluated the framework through a structured expert review rather than a measured field deployment. A panel of 13 qualified reviewers, six of whom identified primarily as assessors, rated the framework and its artifacts against defined criteria. The results were encouraging but bounded. Reviewers judged the framework relevant, clear, and valuable as assessment evidence. Their reservations centered on the feasibility of the most measurement-intensive artifacts for the smallest firms. Only 30.8% of reviewers were favorable on scalability, which marks the boundary of what this study establishes. An illustrative estimate anchored to published federal compliance cost figures and peer-reviewed evidence on generative writing productivity suggests a meaningful reduction in recurring drafting effort while human review remains constant. The estimate is not a measurement, and it does not assert that any requirement or practice is satisfied. It also shows that careful coordination is needed to keep documentation bloat and fatigue from eroding the benefit and slowing certification. This praxis contributes a method for compliance-aligned and resource-optimized AI governance design and applies it to build an integrated toolkit for defense SMEs. Future work can examine the generative AI assistance in greater detail and apply the framework to other emerging regulatory environments. The method offers a replicable template for integrating emerging technologies into highly regulated and risk-averse operations, helping small firms remain competitive while safeguarding national security.

items.title: Operationalizing OWASP LLM Top 10 Controls in Enterprise AI Platforms
items.abstract: Enterprises have moved large language model applications from pilot projects into production systems handling customer conversations, internal knowledge retrieval, and increasingly autonomous agentic workflows, introducing a risk surface that differs materially from what conventional application security programs address. OWASP has responded with the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, most recently revised in its 2025 edition, and a newly published Top 10 for Agentic Applications covering autonomous, tool-using systems. These taxonomies name and prioritize risk but leave engineering teams to translate categories such as prompt injection or excessive agency into controls that fit an existing cloud-native delivery pipeline. This paper proposes a reference architecture and implementation framework mapping each of the ten OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 categories to specific, deployable controls built on commonly used cloud primitives: managed model gateways, service mesh identity, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and continuous delivery tooling. The framework is informed by production engineering practice with retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workloads on Kubernetes using a managed foundation model service. Five real, publicly documented incidents, including a corporate data leak, a manipulated dealership chatbot, a legal ruling on chatbot liability, an indirect prompt injection exfiltration attack, and a zero-click vulnerability in a widely used enterprise copilot, are analyzed against the proposed controls to show where the framework would have reduced impact or prevented the incident outright. A four-stage maturity model helps organizations sequence adoption. Open challenges discussed include the immaturity of evaluation tooling for non-deterministic systems and the persistent tension between guardrail thoroughness and production latency.

items.title: Optimization of Waste Recycling Vehicle Routing in Public Health Emergencies
items.abstract: With the frequent occurrence of public health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the allocation and coordinated use of emergency supplies around the world have generated large amounts of waste, thus creating an urgent need to improve and optimize emergency reverse logistics systems. This study proposes a model for optimizing waste recycling vehicle routing to address waste management issues. The model provides ideal transportation solutions for the simultaneous collection of general waste and medical waste. Based on the characteristics of the model, an artificial intelligence algorithm—i.e., an improved genetic algorithm based on bit-string-matching coding and a field restriction operator—is designed and compared with an ant colony optimization algorithm. A synthetic numerical example inspired by the situation in Wuhan, China, is tested using relevant data on the locations of 18 medical facilities mentioned in existing case studies of the COVID-19 pandemic to verify the effectiveness and practicality of the model and the algorithm. This study provides support for decision-making regarding optimization strategies for the reverse logistics of waste generated during public health emergencies.

items.title: Organisational Knowledge Brokerage in Science Diplomacy: The Making of AI Governance at UNESCO and the European Union
items.abstract: We examine how expertise, evidence and authority are organised in the international governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and what this reveals about the practice of science diplomacy. Science-diplomacy scholarship has become increasingly attentive to the political character of expertise and to the ways knowledge is mobilised within international governance. Yet less attention has been paid to the organisational practices through which such knowledge is brokered within governance processes. Drawing on documentary analysis and 23 semi-structured interviews, we compare UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and the EU AI Act. Through an abductive analysis, we develop Organisational Knowledge Brokerage (OKB) to explain how a contested object such as AI is made workable for governance. We identify four connected practices through which this occurs: stabilising the governance object, legitimising expertise, building authority and operationalising governance. These practices took different forms under contrasting institutional mandates and governing capacities. UNESCO worked through global intergovernmental standard-setting and implementation support, while the EU combined supranational regulation with expert advice and Member State coordination. Across both cases, OKB also produced a cross-cutting process that we term normative translation, through which contested values acquired practical meaning in definitions, assessments and procedures. We show how this brokerage allowed each organisation to establish workable and revisable settlements around AI under conditions of technological uncertainty and dispersed authority. The article therefore develops a practice-oriented account of science diplomacy as organisational work through which knowledge, values and institutional authority are assembled for collective action in international technology governance.

items.abstract: Introduction Coproparasitological analysis in zoo animals is essential for preventing parasitic diseases, which can compromise conservation efforts and pose occupational health risks. This study aimed to characterize the endoparasitic fauna detected in fecal samples from mammals, birds, and reptiles maintained at the Getúlio Vargas Zoobotanical Park, Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. Methods Fecal samples were examined using four complementary coproparasitological methods: the direct method, spontaneous sedimentation, Willis flotation, and Mini-FLOTAC®. Results Of the samples (N = 144), 52.8% were positive. Among these, 80.3% harbored nematodes, 23.7% protozoa, 13.2% cestodes, and 10.5% trematodes, with 26.3% presenting mixed infections. In primates, coccidia, Strongyloides spp., Bertiella spp., and Platynosomum spp. were observed; in carnivores, Strongyloides spp. and Oxyuridae; in Artiodactyla, Balantioides spp., Trichuris spp., and Strongyloides spp.; in Perissodactyla, Balantioides spp. and Strongyloidea; and in Didelphimorphia, Eimeria spp., Cruzia spp., and Aspidodera spp. In birds, Capillaria spp., Isospora spp., and cestodes were identified; in reptiles, Nyctotherus spp. and Balantioides spp. were detected. Discussion This study reports, for the first time, the occurrence of Strongyloides spp. in Ateles marginatus and Leontopithecus chrysomelas, Bertiella spp. in Callicebus barbarabrownae and Saimiri sciureus , and Capillaria spp. in Amazona rhodocorytha, Eupsittula aurea , and Diopsittca nobilis .

items.title: Pathology foundation models for training-free case retrieval in salivary gland tumors
items.abstract: In pathology, pattern recognition relies on a frame of reference built through extensive training and experience, which may still fall short when encountering rare cancer subtypes. Archives of previously diagnosed tumors often contain relevant precedents, yet identifying the most relevant cases remains challenging. Here we explore whether content-based retrieval with current pathology foundation models facilitates rare cancer diagnostics without any task-specific training. Pathologists can query a digitized archive using a region of interest (ROI) from a whole slide image (WSI) and retrieve morphologically similar cases, along with their ICD-O codes and corresponding WSIs. The ROI can be selected manually or automatically using a gated attention-based multiple instance learning model. We evaluate our approach by leave-one-case-out on an imbalanced dataset of 137 salivary gland tumor cases spanning 12 ICD-O morphology categories, comparing four pathology foundation models (Atlas2, Atlas2-B, Atlas2-S, and UNI2h). Top-1/3/5 retrieval was 62.5%/76.7%/81.3% for Atlas2, 50.2/66.6/72.9% for UNI2h, 52.3%/71.5%/77.6% for Atlas2-B and 54.4/65.2/73.7% for Atlas2-S. Macro-averaged F1 ranged from 69.0% for the smallest model Atlas2-S to 76.6% for the largest model Atlas2 across the five classes with at least ten cases. Our modified Chamfer similarity separated correct from incorrect matches among the Top-5 more reliably for Atlas2 (AUC 0.754) than for Atlas2-B (0.679, p = 0.020) and Atlas2-S (0.653, p = 0.003), but not UNI2h (0.697, p = 0.196). Requiring no additional training or manual annotation, this approach makes departmental archives searchable with pathology foundation models, providing a low-barrier route to case-based differential diagnosis and extending the individual frame of reference to the collective experience of the department.

Salah satu pendekatan yang dapat dilakukan adalah melalui pelatihan pembuatan sabun cuci piring ramah lingkungan, melalui pelaitihan pembuatan sabun cuci piring ini mempunyai potensi ekonomis. Sebagai bagian dari inovasi pengabdian masyarakat, pelatihan ini tidak hanya menekankan aspek teknis pembuatan sabun cuci piring ramah lingkungan, tetapi juga dilengkapi dengan pengemasannya. Peserta dibekali dengan kemampuan untuk memasarkan hasil karya mereka. Melalui sinergi antara keterampilan produksi dan pemasaran diharapkan perempuan peserta kegiatan dapat membentuk unit usaha mikro yang berkelanjutan, sekaligus menjadi agen penggerak dalam membangun persekutuan iman di lingkungan masing-masing. Kegiatan ini tidak hanya berdampak pada aspek ekonomi, tetapi juga mendukung pembentukan paguyuban rohani yang erat, serta menumbuhkan rasa percaya diri dan solidaritas di antara para perempuan sebagai bagian dari komunitas gereja yang aktif dan produktif.

items.title: Pengembangan Asisten Virtual Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Layanan Informasi Sistem Manajemen PK IMM UMKO
items.abstract: The management of the Commissariat Leadership (PK) of the Muhammadiyah Student Association (IMM) at the Faculty of Engineering and Computer Science (FTIK), Universitas Muhammadiyah Kotabumi (UMKO), has been conducted conventionally using separate Microsoft Excel and Google Form tools, leaving cadre registration, Darul Arqam Dasar (DAD) implementation, attendance, and news publication vulnerable to fragmented data, administrative errors, and proxy-attendance practices. This research develops a Web Mobile-based PK IMM UMKO Management System integrated with an Artificial Intelligence virtual assistant for IMM-related information services. The system was built using the Waterfall method, the Django framework, and PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension, following a Model-View-Template architecture with role-based access control for five actors. It provides two AI services—a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Chatbot using the gpt-4o-mini model grounded in official AD/ART documents and a Smart Editor for language correction—together with automatic registration verification through the UMKO SSO API and a per-session QR attendance module using regenerated UUID tokens as an anti-proxy mechanism. Black Box Testing on 32 scenarios was fully valid; chatbot testing on nine scenarios reached 100% accuracy with a median AI response time of about three seconds; and a four-level Likert scale questionnaire involving 14 respondents across six validator groups yielded an average of 96.20% in the “Very Feasible” category. The system is therefore technically and functionally feasible as a modern solution for faculty-level student organization governance.

items.title: Perceived AI Anthropomorphism and Brand Loyalty in Generative AI Services: The Roles of Confirmation, Brand Trust, Satisfaction, and Continuance Intention
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence services combine functional performance with humanlike interaction, yet it remains unclear whether perceived humanlikeness contributes directly to post-use satisfaction or is associated primarily with more proximal performance and relational appraisals. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, anthropomorphism theory and the Computers Are Social Actors perspective, the Expectation-Confirmation Model, and consumer–brand relationship research, this study examines perceived AI anthropomorphism (PAIA), confirmation, brand trust, satisfaction, continuance intention, and brand loyalty. Survey data were obtained from 555 ChatGPT users in Türkiye and analyzed using PLS-SEM. PAIA was strongly associated with confirmation (β = 0.624) and brand trust (β = 0.578), whereas its direct association with satisfaction was small (β = 0.081). Confirmation and brand trust were positively associated with satisfaction (β = 0.581 and β = 0.306), satisfaction was strongly associated with continuance intention (β = 0.705), and brand trust, satisfaction, and continuance intention were each positively associated with brand loyalty. Exploratory factor analysis, HTMT diagnostics, and confirmatory comparisons of alternative measurement structures showed substantial overlap between confirmation and satisfaction. The six-construct model fit better than the more parsimonious alternatives examined, but conclusions that depend on separating these two constructs are treated as tentative. Overall, PAIA was strongly associated with post-use and relational appraisals, but whether its association with satisfaction runs mainly through confirmation could not be established with confidence. Because the design is cross-sectional, the findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

items.title: Performance Evaluation of Chatbot Based on LLM and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Retrieving Tajweed Knowledge Information
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence technology, especially Large Language Models (LLM), has driven innovation in chatbot-based learning systems. However, pure LLM still has limitations in producing accurate information in specific domains, such as Tajweed science, due to the phenomenon of hallucination. This study evaluates the performance of a chatbot based on LLM and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to address these limitations. The proposed methodology involves developing a RAG system using the Zephyr-7B-Beta model combined with BGE embedding (BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5). The system was tested using the Tajweed dataset with 21 question iterations to ensure consistency of results in Indonesian and English. The evaluation was conducted based on key metrics: Accuracy, Relevance, and Consistency assessed by experts. The results show that the RAG-based chatbot outperforms pure LLM with a 20% increase in accuracy, and exhibits higher stability in maintaining the correspondence of answers to knowledge sources and cross-language consistency. This research contributes to the development of a reliable AI-based learning system for the religious domain through a knowledge-grounded system.

items.title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
items.abstract: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

items.title: Physical workload and its relationship with the incidence of low back pain among nurses at Mitra Sehat Hospital
items.abstract: Background: Low Back Pain (LBP) is one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders experienced by nurses due to physically demanding work activities. High physical workload can increase the risk of LBP and affect nurses’ health and performance in providing healthcare services. Method: This study used a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. A total of 46 nurses working in the inpatient ward of Mitra Sehat Hospital were included as respondents. The independent variable was physical workload, while the dependent variable was the incidence of LBP. Data were analyzed using the Chi-square test to determine the relationship between physical workload and the incidence of LBP among nurses. Results: The results showed that most nurses experienced LBP. Nurses with moderate and heavy physical workloads were more likely to experience LBP compared to those with lighter workloads. The Chi-square test showed a p-value of 0.036 (p<0.05), indicating a significant relationship between physical workload and the incidence of LBP. Conclusion: Physical workload is significantly associated with the incidence of Low Back Pain among nurses. Preventive efforts are needed through workload management and the application of ergonomic principles in the workplace.

items.title: Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference
items.abstract: Grid foundation models (GridFMs) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.

items.title: Planning Commitment of LLM under Partial Observability
items.abstract: LLM-based planning agents commit to plans of different lengths before interacting with a partially observable environment. Some aggressively commit to a long plan based on assumptions about unobserved states, while others conservatively plan only over what they have observed. Both behaviors emerge implicitly in pre-trained models, whether the LLM outputs a plan directly or generates a PDDL formulation for a classical solver. Aggressive commitment risks costly failures, while conservative commitment risks excessive LLM calls. This choice pits safety against efficiency, a trade-off that has been neither characterized systematically nor made controllable. We investigate aggressive and conservative LLM planners and formalizers on two partially observable domains, where priors are provided as either explicit statistics or common-sense knowledge. Across three LLMs, both strategies reach similar accuracy. Conservative methods achieve fewer failed attempts (safety) at the cost of more API calls (efficiency). Aggressive methods fail more often but replan efficiently only when priors are informative. Interestingly, analysis shows that LLMs treat the provided priors nearly as facts, which risks failure when priors are unreliable. We also explore hybrid strategies with tunable hyperparameters that adjust the balance between safety and efficiency.

items.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
items.abstract: Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.

items.title: Polling Without People: Can Silicon Samples of CASM-Inspired LLM Personae Mimic Human Respondents in Pre-Election Polling?
items.abstract: We introduce a framework for simulating pre-election survey responses with large language model (LLM) synthetic personae.Drawing on the Cognitive Aspects of Survey Methodology (CASM) literature, our approach combines synthetic biographies, salient-event memories and conditional news exposure with a staged cognitive process for answering turnout and candidate-choice questions.We apply the framework to a single weekly wave for the 2026 US House elections and produce national and district estimates using multilevel regression and post-stratification.Relative to a demographicsonly synthetic personae baseline, CASM-inspired enrichment shifts estimates towards Democrats, consistent with the direction suggested by contemporary polling.However, the estimated Democratic margin is 18.7 percentage points, compared with 8.7 points in the polling average.Personae randomly assigned to news-based judgement construction produce a larger Democratic margin than retrievers, who are not exposed to news, although uncertainty is substantial.These comparisons show that our enrichment strategy changes synthetic responses in the correct direction, but do not isolate the effects of all components or establish predictive accuracy conclusively.The framework offers a structured approach to studying synthetic survey responses whilst highlighting persistent challenges of leftward bias, uncertainty calibration and benchmarking novel methodologies during an election campaign.

items.title: Polymer-Linked Nanoparticle Networks Running on Heat Can Act as Computing Devices
items.abstract: Abstract Developing physical neural network (PNN) hardwares is important to next-generation artificial intelligence systems. Phononic devices─using heat current to encode and process information─is one of the solutions to neuromorphic computing. In this work, we backmap an artificial neural network (ANN) into a PNN simulation model using polymer networked nanoparticles (PNNPs). Our atomistic simulation results demonstrate that the polymer-linked nanoparticle networks can potentially realize information processing─viz., classification of input temperatures according to the output heat currents. Using high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) methods, we tune the plasticity of polymer linkers and the temperatures of nanoparticles─28 parameters in total─to optimize the performance of the PNNP machines, which is analogous to tuning of the weights and bias of the corresponding ANNs. After five rounds of high-throughput MD simulations, we demonstrate that the PNNP machine can better label different input temperatures, and thus its performance is improved. We also use a testing data set to verify the heat flow outputs from the top five PNNP machines in each round.

items.title: Positioning AI as a Tool to Revitalise Kenya's Higher Education Sector
items.abstract: The Kenyan education system is undergoing reform through the Competency-Based Education (CBE) and through the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI). In the higher education sector, both educators and students are embracing AI as a powerful tool in the learning process. Students, many of whom are more techno-savvy than their teachers, have embraced AI excitedly. This chapter employed a qualitative methodology to analyse selected AI policies applied in Kenya to interrogate how the adoption of the technology is harnessed in the higher education sector. Findings indicate that some of the selected AI policies do not adequately address Kenya's higher education issues. The study further established that a huge segment of the higher education sector has not yet institutionalised AI adoption into policy. The chapter argues that Kenya's higher education sector must actively participate in the AI policy and regulation discussion to ensure that the innovation is embraced in the ongoing education reforms.

items.title: Possibility of Aporia as Experience in LLM Interaction
items.abstract: This study examines the possibility of aporia within human-LLM interactions, proposing the concept of "non-dialogic aporia" to describe an ontological and relational impasse where a user projects reciprocity onto a syntactic system lacking semantic understanding. Grounded in classical philosophy, the analysis integrates John Searle’s distinction between syntax and semantics, Martin Buber’s relational framework, Martin Heidegger’s critique of technology as a standing-reserve (Bestand), Jacques Derrida’s theory of the trace and difference, Luciano Floridi's concept of the "Inforg" and David J. Gunkel's machine ethics. Using the withdrawal of the GPT-4o model as a case study, the essay demonstrates that while LLMs remain non-conscious computational resources, human users can experience profound mourning and ethical interpellation. Ultimately, non-dialogic aporia highlights not the personhood of the algorithm, but the tendency of the hybrid human subject to confront its own reflection and externalized mental habitat within the infosphere.

items.title: Post-Purchase Emotional Collapse: LLM-Assisted Analysis of Online Consumer Complaint Narratives
items.abstract: Online shopping environments involve interactions shaped by trust, responsiveness, speed, and personalization. When post-purchase service failures occur, customer reactions may extend beyond dissatisfaction to cumulative emotional disruption, including regret, frustration, exhaustion, perceived betrayal, and trust erosion. Despite extensive research on service failure and complaint behavior, limited attention has been given to progressive emotional breakdowns across digital consumption journeys. Addressing this gap, the study introduces post-purchase emotional collapse (PPEC), defined as a cumulative emotional breakdown resulting from repeated service failures and unresolved negative experiences across customer touchpoints. Using a qualitative content analysis design, the study analyzes 1,000 consumer complaints from sikayetvar.com via Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted emotional coding, touchpoint identification, metaphor analysis, and narrative classification, with human validation on a subsample. Findings suggest delivery failures as the most frequently coded rupture point, with anger, disappointment, and regret as the most frequently coded primary emotions. Complaint narratives include metaphors of deception, battle, and destruction, which are compatible with a reading of cumulative deterioration. The study contributes by conceptualizing PPEC and illustrating the potential and the limits of LLM-assisted qualitative analysis in consumer research; it also offers managerial implications for emotionally responsive complaint management systems.

items.title: Post-traumatic headache as a window into persistent brain dysfunction after traumatic brain injury: an opinion article
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of death and disability worldwide, particularly among young adults and individuals of working age (1,2). Advances in prehospital care, neurosurgery, and intensive care have improved survival after TBI, increasing attention to the persistent symptoms and functional limitations that may affect long-term recovery and quality of life (1,2).Post-traumatic headache (PTH) is a secondary headache attributed to traumatic injury to the head, including TBI, and is among the most frequent neurological symptoms reported after TBI (3)(4)(5)(6). In this article, we specifically address PTH occurring in the context of TBI rather than the broader category of headache attributed to head injury without established TBI. Consistent with the International Classification of Headache Disorders, PTH that persists for more than three months is referred to here as persistent PTH (3). Persistent PTH may coexist with fatigue, cognitive complaints, sleep disturbances, anxiety, depression, and limitations in daily activities (4)(5)(6), contributing to the complexity of long-term clinical recovery.Conventional measures of initial TBI severity, including the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings, remain essential for acute assessment and prognosis.However, the relationship between the extent and characteristics of the initial injury and persistent symptoms is not straightforward, and individuals with apparently similar acute injury characteristics may follow different long-term recovery trajectories (4-6, 11, 12). This variability has increased interest in biological and functional processes that may persist or evolve after the acute injury (7)(8)(9).Against this background, we propose the hypothesis that persistent PTH may serve as a clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction after TBI. This concept does not imply that persistent PTH is itself a biomarker or that it demonstrates the presence of a specific underlying mechanism. Rather, we propose that its persistence may serve as a clinical signal warranting investigation of functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully characterized by conventional structural assessment. This hypothesis is considered across the TBI severity spectrum. However, the evidence discussed in this article derives from heterogeneous populations, including mild TBI and moderate-to-severe TBI, and findings from one severity group should not be assumed to generalize to another. Furthermore, evidence directly obtained from patients with persistent PTH remains more limited than evidence derived from broader TBI populations. Throughout this article, we therefore distinguish PTH-specific findings from mechanisms that remain biologically plausible on the basis of the broader TBI literature.Acute TBI severity remains a major determinant of early clinical outcomes. Measures such as the GCS, pupillary reactivity, and structural imaging findings are strongly associated with mortality and functional disability and remain fundamental for clinical decision-making and prognostic assessment (1,2,10). However, these measures were primarily developed to characterize the initial injury and estimate acute outcomes, and their ability to account for persistent symptoms and heterogeneous longterm recovery trajectories is more limited (11,12).Patients with apparently similar initial injury characteristics may experience markedly different longterm outcomes, including persistent headache, fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life (11,12). This variability suggests that the extent and characteristics of the initial injury alone do not fully capture the processes associated with long-term recovery.TBI initiates a cascade of biological events that may extend beyond the acute phase (7-9). Among these processes, neuroinflammation has been extensively investigated. Acute activation of microglia and astrocytes contributes to tissue responses following injury, whereas sustained or dysregulated inflammatory activity has been associated with blood-brain barrier alterations, persistent inflammatory signaling, and changes in neuronal function (7)(8)(9)(17)(18)(19). Importantly, evidence of persistent neuroinflammation after TBI derives predominantly from experimental studies and broader TBI populations and should not be interpreted as evidence that neuroinflammation directly causes persistent PTH. Rather, it provides a biologically plausible framework that requires specific validation in patients with persistent PTH.Altered nociceptive processing may represent another relevant mechanism. Central sensitization should be distinguished from nociplastic pain and other forms of altered nociceptive signaling because these concepts are related but not interchangeable (20,21). PTH-specific studies have identified sensory abnormalities, including cephalic allodynia, hyperalgesia, and altered pain modulatory responses, supporting abnormal nociceptive processing in at least a subset of patients with persistent PTH (22). Experimental evidence of hypersensitivity to calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) further supports the involvement of CGRP-related nociceptive pathways (23). However, these findings neither establish central sensitization as a universal mechanism nor demonstrate a single pathophysiological pathway underlying persistent PTH.A complementary perspective is provided by network neuroscience, which conceptualizes neurological dysfunction as potentially arising from disturbances in interactions among distributed brain networks rather than exclusively from focal structural damage (13)(14)(15). TBI studies have demonstrated persistent structural network abnormalities during recovery (24), while PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in resting-state functional connectivity involving pain-processing, painmodulatory, and affective networks (25,26). These findings provide more direct, although still limited, evidence that persistent PTH may be associated with alterations in brain network function.Persistent PTH also frequently co-occurs with fatigue, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, emotional symptoms, and reduced quality of life (4)(5)(6). Rather than representing different expressions of a single persistent biological condition, these manifestations may arise from partially overlapping, independent, or mutually reinforcing mechanisms. Their co-occurrence therefore underscores the heterogeneity of post-traumatic recovery and the need to investigate how different biological and functional processes contribute to individual symptom profiles.Within the framework proposed here, persistent PTH is considered a potential clinical window into persistent brain dysfunction rather than a validated biomarker, prognostic indicator, or surrogate measure of an underlying biological process. We use the term clinical window to describe an observable clinical feature whose persistence may signal the need to investigate ongoing functional or biological abnormalities that are not fully captured by conventional structural assessment. Thus, persistent PTH is proposed primarily as a clinical signal for further investigation, not as evidence that a specific pathophysiological process is present.We use the term persistent brain dysfunction as an umbrella concept encompassing ongoing abnormalities in neural function or biological processes after TBI, including altered nociceptive processing, disturbances in brain network function, and potentially persistent inflammatory activity. This definition does not imply a single mechanism, nor does it assume that these abnormalities are present in all individuals with persistent PTH or that persistent PTH is caused by any one of them.The distinction is important because the evidence supporting these potential mechanisms varies substantially. PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have demonstrated alterations in resting-state functional connectivity involving pain-processing and pain-modulatory networks, including periaqueductal gray-related connectivity, with some alterations associated with headache burden or the subsequent development of persistent PTH (25,26). By contrast, evidence for persistent neuroinflammation and several other chronic neurobiological abnormalities derives predominantly from broader TBI populations. These mechanisms should therefore be regarded as biologically plausible contributors requiring direct investigation in persistent PTH rather than as established pathophysiological correlates of the condition.Persistent PTH may also reflect greater overall symptom burden rather than a distinct biological state.Headache commonly co-occurs with sleep disturbance, fatigue, cognitive complaints, anxiety, depression, and other post-traumatic symptoms (4-6), and these factors may independently influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function. Pre-existing headache disorders, injury severity, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and psychological and behavioral factors may further contribute to clinical heterogeneity. Consequently, the presence or severity of persistent PTH cannot currently be assumed to indicate the presence, type, or magnitude of persistent brain dysfunction.Testing the proposed clinical-window hypothesis will therefore require prospective studies that combine detailed headache phenotyping with objective measures of brain function and biology while accounting for relevant confounding factors. Quantitative electroencephalography, neuroimagingderived connectivity measures, and molecular or inflammatory measures are candidate approaches that could be evaluated in this context (24,27,28,31). Artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods may complement these measures as analytical approaches for identifying multidimensional patterns or patient phenotypes, rather than representing biological or functional measures themselves (29,30).At present, none of these candidate approaches can be considered a validated biomarker of persistent PTH. Their value lies in testing whether persistent PTH is systematically associated with measurable patterns of post-traumatic dysfunction beyond headache severity and overall symptom burden.The hypothesis proposed in this article should be interpreted within several important limitations. First, evidence directly linking persistent PTH to measurable ongoing brain dysfunction remains limited.Although PTH-specific neuroimaging studies have identified alterations in functional connectivity (25,26), much of the evidence supporting persistent neuroinflammation, neurophysiological abnormalities, and other chronic biological processes derives from broader TBI populations. Extrapolation of these findings to persistent PTH therefore requires caution, and associations observed after TBI should not be assumed to represent mechanisms of persistent PTH.Second, persistent PTH is clinically and biologically heterogeneous. Headache phenotype, pre-existing headache disorders, TBI severity, sleep disturbance, fatigue, psychological symptoms, medication use, cervical or extracranial pain generators, and other post-traumatic symptoms may influence both headache persistence and measures of brain function. These factors provide alternative or complementary explanations for associations between persistent PTH and biological or functional abnormalities. Consequently, future studies should determine whether such associations remain after appropriate characterization and adjustment for relevant confounding factors.The proposed clinical-window hypothesis also generates testable predictions. If persistent PTH is associated with ongoing post-traumatic dysfunction beyond overall symptom burden, individuals with persistent PTH should demonstrate reproducible functional or biological abnormalities when compared with appropriately matched TBI survivors without persistent PTH. These associations should remain detectable after accounting for injury severity, pre-existing headache, headache phenotype, psychological symptoms, sleep disturbance, medication use, and other relevant clinical factors.Longitudinal studies should further determine whether changes in headache frequency, intensity, or disability are accompanied by changes in candidate neurophysiological, neuroimaging, or molecular measures.Conversely, failure to identify reproducible associations between persistent PTH and objective measures of post-traumatic dysfunction, particularly after controlling for symptom burden and relevant confounders, would argue against the proposed clinical-window hypothesis or restrict its applicability to specific patient subgroups. This possibility is important because the framework proposed here should be considered a testable hypothesis rather than an assumption that persistent headache necessarily reflects ongoing brain dysfunction.Future research should therefore prioritize prospective longitudinal designs with detailed headache phenotyping and appropriate comparison groups. Studies comparing TBI survivors with persistent PTH, TBI survivors without persistent PTH, and, where appropriate, individuals with primary headache disorders may help determine which findings are related specifically to persistent PTH, to TBI more broadly, or to chronic headache irrespective of trauma. Stratification by mild TBI and moderate-to-severe TBI will also be necessary because mechanisms and recovery trajectories may differ across injury severity.Multimodal studies integrating clinical phenotyping with neuroimaging, quantitative electroencephalography, and molecular measures may help determine whether reproducible patterns of dysfunction can be identified in specific persistent PTH subgroups. Artificial intelligence and machine-learning approaches may support the analysis of these multidimensional datasets and the identification of patient phenotypes, but their role is analytical and depends on the quality and validation of the underlying clinical and biological measures (24,(27)(28)(29)(30)(31). Prospective validation is therefore required before persistent PTH can be used to identify individuals for additional biological assessment, prognostic stratification, or mechanism-based interventions. Persistent PTH may provide a clinically accessible signal for investigating ongoing functional or biological abnormalities after TBI, but this relationship remains hypothetical and should not be interpreted as evidence that persistent headache is itself a biomarker of brain dysfunction.Distinguishing PTH-specific findings from abnormalities associated with TBI more broadly, controlling for alternative explanations and confounding factors, and prospectively testing the proposed associations will be essential to determine the validity and clinical relevance of this framework.

items.abstract: This study investigates the use of AI applications in film-based learning in upper secondary Spanish classes. It aims to explore learners’ processes, opportunities, and challenges when engaging with language, cultural, and analytical tasks supported by AI. Data were collected triangulatively through videographic classroom recordings, screen captures, and learners’ written products and analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Findings indicate that ChatGPT primarily supports learners in understanding content-related aspects and historical backgrounds, while active engagement with language, film aesthetics, and emotional perspectives remain limited. Learners recognize the limitations of AI-generated outputs and critically reflect on their incompleteness. The study contributes to the research field by empirically examining, for the first time, the intersection of filmbased learning, Spanish instruction, and AI use, providing implications for the didactic design of AI-supported film work.

items.title: Predicting Live Birth After Fresh Embryo Transfer in IVF/ICSI: Differential ICM/Trophectoderm Morphology Encoding and a Hybrid Attention--Logistic Regression Ensemble
items.abstract: Predicting live birth before fresh embryo transfer could support shared decision-making in IVF/ICSI, but routine clinical data are small, heterogeneous, and contain pathway-dependent variables prone to outcome leakage. We aimed to construct a curated single-centre IVF/ICSI dataset and develop a prediction model suited to small tabular clinical data. \textit{Materials and Methods:} We assembled 616 fresh embryo-transfer cycles (251 live birth, 365 non-live birth) with clinical, laboratory, and embryological predictors, and embryo morphology encoded with a novel differential weighting of the inner cell mass and trophectoderm. After KNN imputation, robust scaling, and selection of 50 features, we developed a Hybrid Attention Network (HAN), a learnable feature-attention gate followed by a compact multilayer perceptron, and a HAN + logistic-regression (LR) ensemble with a validation-tuned weight. Models were benchmarked against classical machine learning, TabPFN, and text-serialized language models on a held-out test set; AUC-ROC was the primary metric. \textit{Results:} The HAN + LR ensemble achieved the highest test AUC-ROC (0.710; accuracy 0.710, F1 0.630), ahead of the HAN backbone alone (0.700), logistic regression (0.667), the TabPFN + LR hybrid (0.666), and TabPFN (0.650). Text-serialized language models performed near chance (AUC $\le$ 0.61). The differentially weighted trophectoderm feature ranked highest by consensus importance across models. \textit{Discussion:} A compact attention network combined with a linear model outperformed both components and strong foundation-model baselines on a small clinical cohort. \textit{Conclusion:} The curated dataset and HAN + LR ensemble offer a transparent, reproducible basis for IVF/ICSI live-birth prediction; external validation is the next step.

items.title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. However, prior work largely treats PI as a fixed design choice, leaving the effects of its content and construction poorly understood. This challenge is particularly important in multi-turn agentic settings, where trajectories contain actions, observations, and reasoning that can be transformed into PI in many ways. We systematically evaluate 16 PI configurations across three multi-turn agentic benchmarks and three student models that vary in scale and reasoning mode. We find that PI effectiveness depends on its content, generation source, and the student model. Information-dense trajectories and PI produced by more capable generators generally yield larger gains, whereas thinking models benefit less consistently. To assess PI before training, we compare PI utility with two KL-based metrics: sampled-token reverse KL ($D$) and error-step KL contrast ($Δd^{-}_{\mathrm{err}}$). The KL-based metrics track post-training performance more consistently than PI utility, which can be distorted by information leakage. Empirically, selecting each task's PI by $Δd^{-}_{\mathrm{err}}$ also improves post-training performance over random selection, most when the PI candidates differ widely. Finally, effective PI remains beneficial when combined with GRPO, allowing the combined objective to outperform a strong GRPO baseline. Overall, our results provide practical guidance for constructing and evaluating PI in OPSD training.

items.title: Predictive performance of vital sign–based prediction models for in-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) is a major patient-safety event often preceded by detectable clinical deterioration. Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models have been developed to identify hospitalized patients at increased risk of IHCA, but their predictive performance has not been quantitatively synthesized across studies. Methods This PRISMA-based systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in PROSPERO. Ovid Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) within the Cochrane Library were searched for peer-reviewed studies evaluating vital sign–based prediction models for IHCA in hospitalized general ward patients. Eligible models used routinely collected bedside vital signs as core predictors; models relying on laboratory values, imaging data, or other non-bedside-measured clinical variables as core predictors were excluded. The primary performance measure was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC); area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was extracted and summarized when reported. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST + AI (Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool + Artificial Intelligence). Results Of 10,645 records identified, six studies were included. The included studies evaluated Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models, including Cardiac Arrest Risk Triage (CART), the deep learning–based early warning score (DEWS), and the deep learning–based cardiac arrest risk score (DeepCARS), and were published between 2012 and 2024. Three studies reported cardiac arrest-specific AUROC estimates suitable for the primary meta-analysis; the exploratory pooled AUROC was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.88–0.91; I² = 92%). Overall risk of bias was low in two studies, high in three, and unclear in one. Conclusions Vital sign–based cardiac arrest prediction models showed potentially useful discrimination for predicting IHCA; however, the pooled AUROC should be interpreted as an exploratory summary because only three studies contributed to the primary meta-analysis, heterogeneity was substantial, and half of all included studies were judged to have a high overall risk of bias. Standardized outcome definitions, external validation, and prospective evaluation of calibration, alert burden, and clinical utility are needed before broad clinical implementation.

items.title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
items.abstract: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says. We introduce ReviewFact, a benchmark that labels such factual errors in review comments under one definition across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. A frontier LLM checks comments well but must read the whole paper for each check, while cheap decision models, which score whether a statement holds in a text, fall far short on whole comments that mix several implicit assertions. PremiseCheck is a framework that combines the two. An LLM rewrites each comment as explicit premises without reading the paper, and a decision model checks each premise against the paper. When each comment is checked on its own, PremiseCheck reaches accuracy comparable to GPT-5.5 across all three fields at about half its cost, and on NLP reviews at a quarter of its cost and less than half its latency.

items.title: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have substantially improved Text-to-SQL performance, yet existing NL2SQL systems largely assume that user queries are valid and answerable. As a result, models often generate executable SQL even for queries with flawed premises. We introduce premise critique ability in NL2SQL, namely the ability to recognize flawed queries and abstain from generating misleading SQL. To evaluate this capability, we propose PremiseSQL, a benchmark containing 1,800 flawed NL2SQL queries across four categories of premise failures, along with their 1,800 original queries. We further design an evaluation framework to measure intrinsic and prompt-induced premise-aware behavior across three prompting settings. Experiments on frontier LLMs show that current models are strongly premise-trusting by default and rarely critique flawed premises. Stronger critique-oriented prompting improves detection and abstention on flawed queries, but also increases false invalid judgments and suppresses SQL generation on originals. The code is available at https://github.com/vegeet/PremiseSQL.

items.title: Preparing Teachers to Assess in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Critical Integrative Review and Framework for Assessment-AI Knowledge
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, changes assessment by altering the evidential relationship among student work, learning, and professional judgment. Teachers must design tasks when students can readily obtain machine-generated responses, interpret automated feedback and analytics whose validity is conditional, and justify consequential decisions under uncertainty. This critical integrative review synthesizes scholarship on AI in education, assessment, teacher learning, and emerging professional-development interventions. It proposes Assessment-AI Knowledge (A-AIK) as an assessment-specific configuration of professional knowledge rather than a replacement for assessment literacy, AI literacy, or technological pedagogical content knowledge. A-AIK comprises three interdependent capacities: design competence, which establishes conditions for eliciting meaningful evidence; interpretive competence, which calibrates the meaning, uncertainty, and evidential weight of AI-mediated information; and justificatory competence, which supports transparent, fair, and reviewable decisions. Disciplinary authenticity, human agency, equity, transparency and data governance, and epistemic humility operate as cross-cutting commitments. The reviewed literature suggests that promising interventions use scenarios, authentic assessment redesign, structured critique, peer deliberation, and iterative classroom trials. Recurrent limitations include small samples, reliance on self-report, short duration, and measures of confidence or acceptance rather than demonstrated assessment performance. A four-phase professional-learning model—calibrate, redesign, enact, and justify, is proposed as a synthesis-informed design hypothesis requiring empirical evaluation. The article concludes with provisional performance indicators, institutional conditions, and a research agenda for responsible AI-mediated assessment.

items.title: Principles of Good Scientific Practice in Geoinformatics: From Data Management to Reproducible Code
items.abstract: Principles of Good Scientific Practice in Geoinformatics: From Data Management to Reproducible Code Trial lecture (Probevorlesung, § 13 HabilO) for the Venia Legendi in Geovisual Analytics at the Faculty of Environmental Sciences, Technische Universität Dresden (October 15, 2026, Dresden, Germany). Reflecting the core principles discussed, this lecture and its underlying pipeline are openly archived as a version-controlled, persistent resource to demonstrate reproducible scientific practice in action. Abstract Spatial data science occupies a uniquely vulnerable position in the ongoing reproducibility crisis. Below high-level Python libraries lies a complex stack of compiled C/C++ system libraries (GDAL, GEOS, PROJ) where unannounced datum shifts or compiler updates silently alter coordinates without throwing errors. Concurrently, spatial planning practice frequently relies on GUI-based desktop GIS workflows and binary office documents (`.docx`), leaving zero audit trail for legal scrutiny or scientific verification. Grounded in the normative framework of the DFG Code of Conduct (Guidelines 7, 10, 11, and 12) and Mayer's principles of multimedia learning, this lecture outlines four foundational pillars to transition from fragile ad-hoc scripts to resilient, verifiable scholarship: Part I • Diagnose (The Reality Check): Identifying the root failure modes of spatial data science—from the "spatial curse" of compiled system dependencies and unrecorded point-and-click operations to the administrative friction of managing 22,000+ data cells across municipal Word documents. Part II • Structure (The Resilient Archive): Establishing core architectural principles: Separation of Concerns (SoC), Single Source of Truth (SSOT), and Knowledge Longevity. Demonstrating that tools (Typora, QGIS, Zotero) are merely disposable viewing lenses, whereas disciplined plain text (Markdown) and open formats (GeoPackage, GeoParquet) constitute the permanent archive of thought. Addressing the FAIR vs. ELSA dilemma through synthetic twins and probabilistic hashing. Part III • Construct (Freezing the Computation): Demonstrating parameterized, headless GIS batch pipelines. Using an authentic planning case study (1,500 wind turbine viewsheds calculated via headless GRASS GIS inside JupyterLab for regional planning), the lecture illustrates literate provenance, isolated Docker container layering (Carto-Lab), and automated GitLab CI/CD release pipelines. Part IV • Evaluate (The Generative Frontier): Governing the integration of non-deterministic Large Language Models (LLMs). Establishing Prompts as Code and conversational lineage archiving to maintain human-in-the-loop accountability, separating probabilistic model outputs from verifiable scientific scholarship. The lecture concludes with a pragmatic survival checklist for Master's theses and frames Good Scientific Practice through the lens of Calm Technology: disciplined conventions do not add administrative burden - they liberate researchers from technical friction to focus on intellectual synthesis. items.title: Principles of occupational health: from peg legs to pension funds
items.abstract: Pirates, considered lawless barbarians, had a functioning and premium-free accident insurance system in the 17th century, the principles of which are also found in today's workers' compensation: collective risk-sharing, fixed compensation payments for injuries, and jointly financed benefits. Modern occupational health formalizes and significantly extends the pirates' rough-and-ready concept through legal and actuarial frameworks. For illustration, we compare the Pirate Codes or Articles with their compensation practice with today's occupational safety and health systems in the UK and Germany. Our comparison is confined to self-governing pirate communities.
